question: In 2010, the UN General Assembly recognised the right to safe drinking water and sanitation as a human right1. The European Citizens’ Initiative ‘Right2Water’ and the European Parliament Resolution of 2015 on the follow-up to this initiative called on the Commission to enshrine this right in law2.

The recast Directive on drinking water (Directive (EU) 2020/2184) improved access to water, especially for vulnerable groups3 and the European Water Resilience Strategy of 2025 explicitly recognises access to clean and affordable water as a human right. However, the right has not yet been enshrined in EU primary law. In view of this, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Does it intend to take legislative or other steps (including a possible proposal to amend the Charter of Fundamental Rights or strengthen existing directives) to fully guarantee access to drinking water as a human right?
What additional measures is it planning as part of the Water Resilience Strategy to ensure the universal and effective exercise of this right, especially for vulnerable groups?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.9.2026) The EU legal framework has been strengthened through the recast Drinking Water Directive1, which requires Member States to improve or maintain access to water intended for human consumption for all, with particular attention to vulnerable and marginalised groups.

This Directive needs to be implemented in accordance with the fundamental rights and principles recognised by the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union2 by ensuring full respect for, inter alia, the right to dignity (Article 1) or the right to life (Article 2) and the EU's commitment to a high level of environmental protection (Article 37).

Under the European Water Resilience Strategy3, access to clean and affordable water is presented as a human right and a public good. As part of this Strategy, the Commission is focusing on effective implementation of EU law, support for investment in water infrastructure, reduction of pollution, improved water efficiency and resilience, and better protection of water resources.
The Commission will continue to promote access to safe drinking water, with particular attention to vulnerable groups.
1 Directive (EU) 2020/2184 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2020 on the quality

of water intended for human consumption (recast), OJ L 435, 23.12.2020, p. 1–62. 2 https://www.europarl.europa.eu/charter/pdf/text_en.pdf. 3 https://commission.europa.eu/topics/environment/water-resilience-strategy_en.
